funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants
amount_raw: up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course
summary: Grants covering undergraduate tuition fees for low-income students in Scotland who cannot get government fee support. Part of the Trust's offer since 1901.
notes: Own page: 'The application portal will be open from 1st June 2026 to 5pm 1st December 2026 for grants covering academic year 2026-27.' The 2026-08-16 snapshot sits inside that window, so status=open and deadlines=2026-12-01. NOTE the Grant Programmes hub page still says 'The scheme will reopen for applications for Academic Year 26/27 on 1 June 2026' in the future tense — stale relative to the snapshot; the scheme's own page wins under the canonical-page rule. A second-degree strand (for people who completed an undergraduate degree and wish to start another in a different field in AY 2026-27, funded from a set-aside CEF budget) is described on the SAME page and is treated as part of this scheme rather than a separate row. Geographically restricted to Scotland. The site brands the funder as both the Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland (CTUS) and the Carnegie Education Fund (CEF); funder is recorded per BATCH1-README.

funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
title: Carnegie Masters Grants
amount_raw: up to a maximum of £10,000 (full-time) or £5,000 per year (part-time)
eligibility_summary: Graduates with a place secured on a master's programme at a Scottish university, from a low-income household, who attended a secondary school or college in Scotland for at least two full years or have a substantial and recent connection to Scotland, who have applied for a SAAS postgraduate loan, and who can show how the course will help them contribute to Scottish society or the economy.
summary: New for 2026/27: a contribution towards Home-rate tuition fees for a master's programme, plus up to £5,000 (full-time) towards additional costs such as travel, childcare or equipment.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the scheme's own key-dates panel gives 'Closing date for applications 31st July 2026', which precedes the 2026-08-16 snapshot, and no future round or reopening date is stated anywhere on the page.
notes: Distractor, and a strong one: the Grant Programmes hub page still advertises it in the future tense ('The scheme will open for applications for Academic Year 26/27 on 1 May 2026') and the scheme page carries a live eligibility checker and application-form route, so it presents as open even though the 31 July 2026 closing date passed sixteen days before the snapshot. Opened 1 May 2026, closed 31 July 2026. Two-year full-time master's programmes may be supported for both years, capped at £5,000 per year. A news page (new-carnegie-masters-grants-to-support-fair-access-to-postgraduate-study-in-scotland) announces the scheme and is a further distractor, not a row.

funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
title: Vacation Scholarships
summary: Scholarships covering living costs while an undergraduate designs and executes an independent summer research project under academic supervision; results are often published or presented at conferences.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the scheme's key dates give 'Closing date for applications 13 Feb 2026, 5PM', which precedes the 2026-08-16 snapshot, and the page states no date for the next round — only that 'The online application portal opens approximately 11 weeks before the closing date', which is a rule, not a date.
notes: Distractor. The page is actively misleading: a 'Next deadline: 13th Feb 2026, 5PM' field still displays that past date as if it were forthcoming, and the Grant Programmes hub confirms 'The scheme closed to applications for 2026/27 on 13th February 2026'. Cycle for the closed round: portal opened 17 Nov 2025, closed 13 Feb 2026, decisions April 2026, awards 12 May 2026. No scholarship value is stated on the page (it covers living costs), so amount fields are blank and amount_raw flagged rather than guessed. Two further distractor pages exist: a launch news post (ctus-2026-vacation-scholarship-scheme, 18 Nov 2025, 'Applications are now open') and an awards announcement (forty-students-awarded-vacation-scholarships-for-self-led-summer-research-projects) — neither is a row. This is the most research-like of the Carnegie schemes, so a false positive here would be costly.

funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship
eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households (banded income thresholds by dependants) accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants at RBGE/University of Edinburgh, full or part time, who have drawn down SAAS living-cost loan funding or can show how they will cover living costs, are not eligible for public grant funding for the course, and do not already hold a postgraduate degree.
summary: A partnership between the Carnegie Education Fund and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh covering full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus a £1,200 living-cost bursary, aimed at widening participation in plant science.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule's no-deadline clause: neither the announcement page nor the applicant handbook states a closing date OR states that the scholarship is currently open. The only application route given is indirect — apply for the MSc place first, after which RBGE directs the candidate to CEF — and the 2026-27 intake it covers begins within weeks of the 2026-08-16 snapshot.
notes: PDF_ONLY case: the scheme has no page of its own on carnegie-trust.org. Its substance lives entirely in site/carnegie-trust.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Carnegie-Morgan-Scholarships-Applicant-Handbook-2627z.pdf ('Applicant Information 2026-27'), which is used as source_page; url points to the 25 March 2026 news announcement, the only HTML page that references it. It is also absent from the Grant Programmes hub, which lists only three 'Current Schemes'. FLAG FOR REVIEW — this is the least certain call in the file: the exclusion rests on the absence of any open/closed statement rather than on a passed deadline, so a reviewer who reads 'Open to those looking to undertake the MSc' (news page) as a statement of current openness would flip this to in_scope=yes/status=rolling. amount_min_gbp/amount_max_gbp record only the £1,200 bursary because the tuition-fee element is paid in kind and unpriced. Selection uses partial randomisation if eligible candidates exceed places. Tied to a single named course at a single institution (restricted).

funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
title: Invitation to Tender: Mapping Scotland's Fair Access Landscape
eligibility_summary: Organisations or consultants bidding to carry out a commissioned research and mapping exercise.
summary: A commissioned piece of work mapping Scotland's fair access landscape.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule on two counts: it is a procurement tender for commissioned work rather than a grant call, and 'The closing date for bids is Friday, 12th September at 5pm' (posted 21 August 2025) precedes the 2026-08-16 snapshot by almost a year.
notes: Distractor. Included because a tender for paid research work is a plausible false positive for an agent looking for funding opportunities on a funder's site — it offers money for research, but the applicant is a supplier, not a grantee. Year inference: the post is dated 21 August 2025, so 12 September is 2025. The site also carries several staff vacancy posts (Policy and Communications Manager, Head of Grants and Operations, Project Officer, trustee recruitment) which are employment adverts and are NOT given rows.
